extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists, zoologists, and naturalists studying freshwater sponges (Spongillidae); museum curators and field biologists
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing or using formal taxonomic descriptions/keys for freshwater sponges (Spongilla and allied taxa), including diagnostic characters (morphology of sponge, skeleton, spicules, gemmules), measurements, types, distributions and biological notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule coat structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether gemmules are covered by a thick granular pneumatic coat, by one or more chitinous membranes, or lack a regular pneumatic coat (e.g. 'gemmules are covered with a thick, apparently granular pneumatic coat' vs. 'gemmules without or with irregular pneumatic coat, covered by a chitinous membrane or membranes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgeneric distinctions depend on coat type (e.g. Subgenus Euspongilla: thick granular coat; Subgenus Stratospongilla: chitinous membranes in which gemmule-spicules lie parallel to the surface). Note also presence/absence of an external delicate membrane and whether the coat is 'thick or horny' or 'granular.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule arrangement (single, paired, grouped, adherent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether gemmules are single, bound together in pairs, arranged in free groups or a 'pavement-layer' at the base, free in the sponge, adhere to support, or are fastened together in groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to separate taxa (e.g. gemmules single vs paired vs forming pavement-layer). Note whether gemmules are free or firmly adherent to the support (S. travancorica: adherent, forming a layer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule spicule orientation and arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Orientation of spicules in the gemmule coat: tangential (arranged tangentially), horizontal layers on external membrane, almost horizontal, more vertical than horizontal, irregular directions, or parallel to surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns (tangential vs horizontal vs vertical/irregular) and presence of a horizontal layer of spicules are diagnostic (e.g. S. lacustris: spicules arranged tangentially with a horizontal layer often present; S. cinerea: gemmule-spicules arranged almost horizontally).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foraminal tubule presence and morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence or absence of a foraminal tubule on the gemmule and its form (stout cylindrical, contorted, slender, conical, straight; sometimes multiple tubules; or absent with foraminal cup instead).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key diagnostic character — e.g. S. proliferens: gemmules possess a foraminal tubule (distinguishes it from S. lacustris and S. alba); S. cinerea and S. travancorica have foraminal tubules (slender/straight/conical; sometimes multiple). Note tubule orifice outline and whether more than one foramen is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: General organization of skeleton: reticulate/loose vs moderately dense vs diffuse; presence and prominence of radiating and transverse fibres; presence/absence of basal membrane; presence of horizontal megascleres; amount of spongin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skeleton density and mesh size are diagnostic (e.g. S. alba: moderately dense network with much smaller meshes and little spongin; S. lacustris: reticulate, loose skeleton with slender fibres). Note presence of basal membrane or horizontal megascleres (used in species diagnosis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton-spicule morphology (megascleres)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form of skeleton-spicules: smooth vs spiny/irregular/serrated ('subspined'); length and slenderness, curvature, blunt vs sharply pointed, stout vs slender; relative proportions (length:breadth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microscopic outline and ornamentation are diagnostic (e.g. S. cinerea: skeleton-spicules appear 'subspined' under high power; S. proliferens: long smooth skeleton-spicules length at least 20× breadth). Use high-power observations for minute serration/ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule-spicule morphology (microscleres associated with gemmules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form of gemmule-spicules: length, curvature (sometimes strongly curved or forming semicircles), blunt vs abruptly pointed, cylindrical, ornamentation with spines that may be longer at the ends or middle, and occasional retroversion of spines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns of spination and curvature (e.g. S. lacustris: gemmule-spicules often more strongly curved and spines relatively longer; S. alba: gemmule-spicules bear backwardly directed spines usually more numerous at the ends). These characters often distinguish closely allied taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flesh-spicule morphology and presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence, abundance and form of flesh-spicules in the parenchyma and external membrane: slender vs numerous vs absent; coverage with straight or backwardly directed spines; differences in relative dimensions from gemmule-spicules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence vs presence is diagnostic (e.g. S. alba var. cerebellata: total absence of flesh-spicules). Compare spine distribution (middle vs ends) and relative slenderness to gemmule-spicules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall habit, form and texture of the sponge
rubrics_metrics.description: Macroscopical growth form: branches (long free cylindrical branches drooping when removed), cushions, flat sheets, encrusting forms, filmy layers, hard but brittle vs soft and fragile; surface characteristics (smooth, undulating, hispid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Habit and texture help separate species (e.g. S. lacustris: flat/rounded basal portion with long branches; S. cinerea: large flat sheets without branches; S. proliferens: soft shallow cushions on leaves). Note whether branches are compressed, anastomose, or absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oscula, pores and canal system characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Size and shape of oscula (star-shaped, moderate/large/small), oscular collars (well-developed or not), radiating furrows and canals, presence/absence of inhalent apertures in certain surfaces, and arrangement of external pores (single cells etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oscular/canal features (e.g. S. lacustris: star-shaped oscula with radiating furrows; S. proliferens: oscula moderate, flat with deep cone-shaped collars) are useful field characters. Also note distribution of pores (periphery vs absent from bud ends) during development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coloration and presence of symbiotic/infesting organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Colour of living specimen (bright green, dirty flesh-colour, white, dirty yellow, dark grey) and presence of 'green corpuscles' (chlorophyll-bearing bodies) vs filamentous algal infestation that can give dark green colour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate green corpuscles (intracellular, chlorophyll) which cause bright green colour (e.g. S. lacustris, S. proliferens) from filamentous algal penetration which is harmful and may mimic greening (not beneficial). Absence of green corpuscles distinguishes species such as S. alba.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurements as diagnostic metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative measurements of spicules (lengths and greatest diameters), gemmule diameters, and ranges of these dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise measurements to distinguish species (examples: S. travancorica gives ranges for skeleton-spicule length 0.289–0.374 mm and gemmule diameter 0.272–0.374 mm). Use micrometric data alongside morphology for diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution and habitat context
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorded geographical occurrence (localities, regions, e.g. Eastern India, Burma, Ceylon, Java, Celebes, Bombay Presidency) and specific habitats (ponds that dry up, leaves of water-plants, roots, brackish ponds, backwaters, slightly brackish water).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution and habitat often support identification (e.g. S. cinerea only known from Bombay Presidency). List localities and typical substrata and note elevation or salinity tolerance where given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type specimens and synonymy practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation of type specimens, type localities, museum depositories (Indian Museum, British Museum), and commentary on synonymy (when to avoid referencing obscure earlier names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record where types and co-types are deposited. The author notes that no type can be recognized for S. lacustris as used by recent authors and advises against complicating regional fauna accounts by citing obscure possible synonyms. Follow museum type conventions and be cautious in synonymy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish species by combination of characters (holistic diagnosis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Species are 'closely allied and must be distinguished rather by the sum of their peculiarities than by any one character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on a single character; use an aggregate of morphological, gemmular, skeletal, spicular, colour, and habitat characters. The text gives comparative statements (e.g. S. proliferens differs from S. lacustris and S. alba by having a foraminal tubule and from S. cinerea by colour and smooth skeleton-spicules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variability, varieties, and subspecies evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition and treatment of intraspecific variation, varieties, and subspecies (e.g. S. lacustris subsp. reticulata differs in branch compression, finer skeleton-fibres, longer skeleton- and gemmule-spicules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether forms represent true varieties/subspecies or merely phases; provide comparative notes (morphology, branch production, presence of green corpuscles). Deposit types/co-types in museums and report local abundance and seasonal occurrence when discussing varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductive and developmental characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations on reproductive mode (sexual reproduction rare; reproduction by buds and gemmules), bud morphology and liberation process, presence/seasonality of gemmules, larval associations (e.g. Sisyra larvae), and germination behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe bud formation, osculum formation in developing buds, floating vs sinking buds, production of extra oscula in captivity, and timing (seasonal production). These biological features can support species recognition and ecological understanding.
